official.deadline_central_display: 21 January 2027 (degree programme application period 7-21 January 2027, 3:00 p.m. GMT+2)
official.deadline_note: The scholarship itself has no standalone deadline. The Early Bird deadline is relative: the applicant must accept the study offer and pay the tuition fee within 28 days after the admission decisions are published (for the 2026 intake the final date was 24 April; UTU corrected this window from 30 to 28 days, information updated 10 March 2026). The Merit Scholarship has a separate application round that opens in spring; Admission Services invite all eligible applicants when it opens, and no calendar dates are published.
official.application_cycle: Annual January intake: one application period per year (next round 7-21 January 2027, studies begin in August). Page information is for students admitted in 2026; students admitted in 2025 or before follow the previous scheme at https://www.utu.fi/en/study-at-utu/scholarships-before-2025
official.status_note: The scholarship scheme is in force for students admitted from the 2026 intake onwards and no scholarship covers the first study year. The January 2026 application round has closed; the next application round to the international degree programmes is 7-21 January 2027, with admission offers decided in spring.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The University of Turku Merit Scholarship 'covers 50% of the tuition fee for the next study year' (50% of the second year tuition for master's students; 50% of the second and third year tuition fees for bachelor's students). The Early Bird discount of 2,000 EUR reduces the first-year tuition fee. UTU states plainly: 'It is not possible to get a scholarship to cover the tuition fee for the first year.'

official.citizenship_residency: Tuition fees and scholarship eligibility apply to citizens of countries outside the EU, EEA or Switzerland; exemptions apply to holders of an EU Blue Card in Finland, a permanent residence permit, a continuous (A) residence permit granted on grounds other than studies, a long-term resident's EU residence permit, an EU Family Member's Residence Card, or temporary protection status.
official.international_eligibility: International (non-EU/EEA) students are the intended recipients of the scholarship; EU/EEA and Swiss citizens pay no tuition fee and are not part of the scholarship scheme.
official.duration: Merit Scholarship: awarded for one academic year at a time, covering 50% of the following study year's tuition fee (second year for master's; second and third years for bachelor's), with a separate application for each year. Early Bird discount: a one-off 2,000 EUR reduction of the first-year tuition fee.
official.description: The University of Turku charges tuition fees from all non-EU/EEA citizens and supports its merited and motivated students with scholarships. Since the 2026 intake it is not possible to get a scholarship covering the first study year; instead newly admitted master's students receive an automatic Early Bird discount of 2,000 EUR if they accept their study offer and pay within 28 days, and every student who completes 55 credits with an average of at least 3.0 and at least 4 credits of Finnish is awarded the Merit Scholarship covering 50% of the tuition fee for the following study year.
official.program_type: Merit-based tuition fee reduction awarded during studies, plus an automatic first-year tuition discount (Early Bird)
official.english_requirement: Master's applicants must prove English at the time of application (no conditional admission on language): IELTS Academic overall band 6.5 with each subtest 6.0 or more; TOEFL iBT overall 92 with writing 22 or more if taken before 21 January 2026, or overall 4.5 with each subtest 4.0 or more if taken on or after that date; PTE Academic overall 68 with writing 61 or more; Cambridge C2 Proficiency or C1 Advanced with pass grade A, B or C; or YKI with a minimum score of 5 in all subtests. Exemptions: a bachelor's or higher degree completed in an English-language programme in an EU/EEA or listed country, or a degree from a Finnish higher-education institution. Test results must be attached by the end of the supplementation period (28 January 2027) and remain verifiable afterwards; no exceptions are made for unlisted tests.

applicant_utility.summary: UTU's funding is deliberately back-loaded: you must finance the entire first year yourself (tuition of EUR 10,000-12,000 depending on programme) and only qualify for support once you are enrolled and studying. Newly admitted master's students can take EUR 2,000 off that first bill by accepting the offer and paying in one instalment within 28 days of the admission decision, so the cash needs to be ready the moment results land. After the first year the Merit Scholarship is close to a formality for anyone who keeps pace: 55 ECTS, a 3.0 average and 4 ECTS of Finnish unlock 50% off the next year's tuition, and bachelor's students can repeat that for the third year. Nothing here funds living costs, so budget roughly EUR 800 per month on top of fees.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EU/EEA applicants who can document funds for a full self-financed first year and who are confident they can clear 55 ECTS with a 3.0+ average while picking up Finnish credits.
application_readiness_checklist: Line up the full first-year tuition (EUR 10,000-12,000) plus the funds Migri expects (EUR 9,600 in the bank for programmes of a year or longer) before admission results are published
If admitted to a master's programme, accept the offer at Studyinfo and arrange the single-instalment discounted payment through Flywire inside the 28-day window
Book an accepted English test months ahead; the result must be attached by the end of the January supplementation period and stay verifiable after it
Plan at least 4 ECTS of Finnish into the first-year study plan from the start, since it is a hard gate for the first Merit Scholarship application
Watch for the spring invitation from Admission Services and submit the Merit Scholarship application promptly when it arrives
common_rejection_risks: Applying on the assumption that first-year funding exists; since the 2026 intake no scholarship covers the first study year and none covers living costs
Missing the 28-day Early Bird window because international transfer times through Flywire were not planned in advance
Dropping below 55 ECTS or a 3.0 average in the first study year, which forfeits the Merit Scholarship for the following year
Submitting a language test that is not on UTU's accepted list, or one that can no longer be verified by the deadline; the University states no exceptions will be made
Forgetting the 4 ECTS of Finnish before the first Merit Scholarship application, which blocks an otherwise qualified student
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: First-year tuition of EUR 10,000-12,000 (less the EUR 2,000 Early Bird for master's students), all living costs of roughly EUR 600-900 per month, the tuition-fee payment and refund gaps, flights and settling-in costs, Student Union membership of about EUR 54 per academic year, the Kela student healthcare fee of EUR 35.35 per term, and a laptop plus study materials.
document_audit: Scans of the original degree certificate and transcript plus official English/Finnish/Swedish translations must be attached to the application form; translator-produced copies without the originals are not accepted
Electronic transcripts are only accepted with a verification code/link or an official e-signature; screenshots or self-downloaded PDFs from the student portal are rejected
Certified true copies do not count as originals unless issued by the awarding institution or the Finnish Digital and Population Data Services Agency
Keep the English test result verifiable past the application period and avoid combined MyBest-style TOEFL scores, which UTU does not accept
alerts: Rules depend on your admission cohort: this scheme applies to students admitted from 2026, while students admitted in 2025 or earlier follow the older scheme of full-tuition two- or three-year scholarships
UTU corrected the Early Bird acceptance and payment window from 30 to 28 days in March 2026, so older third-party pages still quoting 30 days are wrong
The Merit Scholarship must be applied for separately each academic year, only when invited by Admission Services in spring; there is no standing open deadline to miss or apply against
US citizens should also check the Fulbright-University of Turku Graduate Award (1000 EUR/month grant plus tuition coverage), which is advertised on the same official page
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply to a UTU bachelor's or master's programme through the January joint application at Studyinfo.fi (7-21 January 2027 for the next intake, supplements by 28 January); if admitted, accept the offer and pay on time to trigger the Early Bird discount, then apply for the Merit Scholarship in spring when Admission Services send the invitation.
